target_customer: Product and growth teams at software companies that already track product analytics events
problem: Product teams drown in dashboards and miss sudden shifts in user behavior metrics unless an analyst watches them. Lantern promised autonomous anomaly detection with no code or configuration.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription (inferred from product positioning; pricing not found)

founders.name: Bastien Beurier
previous_startups: A previous YC company (name not stated on the YC page)
founders.background_notes: Prior roles and repeat founder status as listed on the YC company page. Education not found.

founders.name: Guillaume Lachaud
founders.background_notes: Listed as a founder on the YC page with no background given.

exit.reason: Cause not public. The YC page marks the company Inactive and the original domain lantern.so is now an expired parked page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Autonomous anomaly detection on event streams needed time series modelling and a Segment integration that required about a week of training data per customer, which is standard data engineering with some hard statistics for a small team.

defensibility.rationale: Anomaly detection was a feature that analytics vendors could add, and the team was four people with no stated data lock in or distribution edge.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Mixpanel later shipped its own anomaly detection and alerts as an enterprise feature and Amplitude shipped Anomaly and Forecast, so incumbents did absorb the wedge, but launch dates were not confirmed in sources found.

market_need_then: Segment's 2019 integration page described Lazy Lantern as autonomous anomaly detection for product metrics, suggesting teams wanted alerts without building monitors. No direct spend or customer evidence was found.

branding.domain_note: Used lantern.so (a .so domain, not .com); the registration has since expired per a Namecheap parked page.

identity.voice_and_tone: Plain, autonomy focused pitch: no code, no configuration, no data expertise

rebrands.why: Not stated. The 2019 Launch HN post and Segment page used Lazy Lantern, while YC lists Lantern.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand was found and the name collides with many other companies called Lantern, including another YC company, so it was forgettable and confusable.

outcome_analysis: Lantern, first called Lazy Lantern, sold autonomous anomaly detection on product analytics data and went inactive without any public post mortem, so the cause is not public. The wedge was a feature that Mixpanel and Amplitude later built, and the name collided with many other Lantern companies, which are plausible but unconfirmed contributors.
notes: Latka states Wellthy owns Lazy Lantern, but Wellthy actually acquired a different company, Lantern, the end of life planning platform, so that claim looks like a conflation and is ignored. No funding found in any search; the company's own domain lantern.so is expired. Competitor list left empty because no source dated near August 2019 was found that names rivals; Mixpanel anomaly detection and Amplitude Anomaly Forecast launch dates were not confirmed. Founder education not found.
